name: Quiet luxury
summary: A tonal room of costly materials and no logos. One hue family in cream, oatmeal, taupe and chocolate covers walls and seats; texture, not colour, gives the variety; pairs of chairs and lamps mirror about the fireplace, and hidden light washes the plaster.

philosophy.core_thesis: Real luxury is the quality of the material and the work, and it does not need to show a name.
design_principles: Use one hue family in 3–5 values, from cream to chocolate; the accent is a darker value of the same hue, not a new hue.
Vary texture, not colour: put at least 4 textures, such as bouclé, cashmere, travertine and walnut, in the seating group.
Mirror pairs of chairs, lamps and side tables about one axis through the fireplace or the bed.
Choose few, large pieces: a deep low sofa of 260–300 cm and a rug of 300 x 400 cm that holds the whole group.
Hide the light sources: cove light, picture light and lamps with opaque shades; no bare bulb is in view.
Use honed, brushed and matt finishes; satin is the highest sheen.
Keep clear routes of 110 cm or more, so that the room never feels full.
anti_patterns: Visible logos, monograms or branded objects
Saturated colour or a second hue family
Gloss lacquer, mirror chrome or high-shine marble
Many small objects and souvenirs on show
Bare bulbs or cool white light
Small, light furniture in a large room

composition.plan_logic: One axis through the fireplace or the bed. Pairs of pieces mirror about it, and one large rug holds the whole group.
composition.focal_point: A stone fireplace or a large abstract painting centred on the axis, lit by a hidden accent.

rules.rule: Centre the fireplace or one large painting on the axis and light it with a hidden accent.
Mirror chairs, lamps and side tables about the axis on the focal wall.
rules.value: 1 axis, 100% mirrored at the focal wall

rules.rule: Give cream the walls, oatmeal and taupe the seats and the rug, and chocolate the accents.
Step the values in small, even steps; no hard black edge.
Hold one hue family and vary the texture of each surface.
Divide the wall panels and the fireplace surround in golden rectangles.
Repeat a wall panel or a moulding at one module.
Compose three planes: a pair of chairs in front, the sofa and table in the middle, the lit focal wall behind.
Put the focal point on the axis of the entrance, so that the view from the door ends on it.
rules.value: door, axis and focal point on 1 line

rules.rule: Leave wide floor around the group and bare wall around the one painting.
Keep generous routes around the rug and behind the sofa.
Wash the walls with a hidden cove, light the art with a picture light, and use a pair of lamps at the sofa; dim all layers.
rules.value: 150 lux ambient, 400 lux task, accent 5:1, 2700 K

rules.rule: Shoot the room level, with a one-point view on the axis from the entrance toward the fireplace.

zoning.circulation: A wide loop around the rug and behind the sofa; no route crosses the seating group.

palette.distribution: Cream plaster on walls and ceiling; oatmeal and taupe on the sofa, chairs and rug; walnut and brushed brass in small amounts; chocolate on one chair, a throw or a vessel.

lighting.strategy: Hidden sources wash the walls and pick out the art. All layers dim; no bulb is in view.
lighting.daylight: Floor-to-ceiling linen sheers on a hidden ceiling track soften the daylight to an even glow.

layers.position: over the painting on the axis

materials.finish: Honed stone, brushed metal, oiled wood and limewash. Satin is the highest sheen; no gloss.
materials.texture_contrast: Smooth honed stone and wood against soft bouclé and cashmere, at about 1:2.

furniture.silhouette: Low, deep pieces in rounded rectangles; plinth bases or short hidden legs; large sizes and soft edges.
furniture.arrangement: Two sofas face each other across the axis of the fireplace, or one sofa faces it with two mirrored lounge chairs.

textiles.pattern: No prints. Texture only: bouclé, herringbone weave, rib knit.
textiles.windows: Floor-to-ceiling linen sheers on a hidden ceiling track, with a fullness of 2 to 2.5 times the window width.

objects.approach: Few and costly: one sculpture, art books, a large ceramic or stone vessel. No logos.
objects.grouping: Pairs on the axis; groups of 3 off the axis, low to high.

implementation.brief: A cream limewash room with a travertine fireplace on the axis. A deep oatmeal bouclé sofa faces it across a travertine table, with two taupe lounge chairs mirrored on the sides; a picture light shows one large abstract painting.
implementation.image_prompt: Quiet luxury living room, cream limewash walls, travertine fireplace centred on the axis, deep low oatmeal bouclé sofa, travertine coffee table, pair of taupe lounge chairs mirrored, pair of ceramic table lamps, large wool rug, one large abstract painting with a brass picture light, floor-to-ceiling linen sheers, tonal palette, soft hidden cove light, architectural digest photograph
implementation.negative_prompt: Logos, saturated colour, gloss, chrome, clutter, bare bulbs, cool light, small furniture, pattern.
implementation.camera: 35 mm lens, camera at 130 cm, one-point view on the axis from the entrance toward the fireplace.
implementation.scene_3d: Room 700 x 550 cm, ceiling 300 cm. 2700 K cove light at the ceiling perimeter; 5:1 spot on the painting; 2 lamps at 2200 K; soft daylight through linen at transmission 0.4.

emotion.target_response: Assured calm: the viewer feels quality in every surface and the confidence of a room that does not need to impress.

avoid_when: The budget does not reach real stone, wool and solid wood; cheap copies break the style.
The brief asks for colour, personality or play.

modifiers.how: Lower the furniture, change travertine to oak and plaster, break the mirror symmetry; keep the tonal palette and matt finishes.
Drench one wall in a saturated hue and add 3 more hues as accents; keep the large, soft pieces.

canonical_works.work: Salon of the Hôtel de Noailles, Paris

sources.title: Pierre-Emmanuel Martin-Vivier, Jean-Michel Frank: The Strange and Subtle Luxury of the Parisian Haute-Monde in the Art Deco Period (Rizzoli, 2008)
Trend evidence, cite only: fashion and interior press used the term from 2022 and 2023
